sectionHeading: #### The first address — to those who would own the world
currentHeading: #### The first address: to those who would own the world
authority: Editorial craft owned by the editorial agent under author delegation. Canon and claim content remain author decisions.

substitutionTest.note: Twenty baseline sentences, 332 words, into 339 words. Eighteen survive in the shipped text, seven of them verbatim, including Suppose you win, Stand in that finished world a moment, Are you happy there, Then aim the fortune there, and We are not asking you to lose. Two were replaced under the corpus voice card, recorded in F2 and F4. Substitution mode is not in effect and the pairing test applies. Chapter-level restoration analysis is in the anchor record v08-15-two-addresses, whose findings F1 and F2 documented this address's earlier seventy-one percent loss and the restoration that repaired it; this record is the child's own account under the twenty-rule standard.

pairedDeletionSweep.outcome: Every cross-referenced term has both ends present in the current volume. The manor is established in Three Dangers and recurs in the strain section and the second address. The demos is quoted in Let the Architects Speak. The lethal edge answers scare enemies and on occasion kill them, which stands in the architects section and returns at the close of the three primal goods. Glad you exist recurs in Appendix B's bonds list. Point the machine toward recurs in Appendix B's long view. No restoration in this section required restoring a severed antecedent, and nothing was reworded to avoid one.

ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0093 requires the addresses to be labeled as addresses rather than as evidence; the italic frame in the parent section does that, and the volume card's direct address override permits this address to invite action without dividing readers into moral camps. Happy, healthy, and holy appears in no debt item, no open canon query, and no current manuscript, so R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD does not fire on its absence; the deletion is nonetheless quoted in F4 because the phrase had a liturgical ring the record should preserve for the author. Nothing else in the ledger governs this section.

findings.summary: Half of the endearment-register cut was applied without being recorded.

evidence.baseline: Darlings — and we mean it tenderly, even to you who are assembling the manor — let us ask you something plainly, founder to founder, soul to soul.
evidence.shipped: To you who are assembling the manor, and we mean this without contempt, let us ask something plainly, founder to founder.

findings.authorizedBy: R-VOICE-BIND. The volume card sets irony as dry and rare, and the corpus card forbids intimacy as a substitute for warrant.
findings.diagnosis: The cut is sound: Darlings and soul to soul are one register, an intimacy performed at the addressee rather than earned, and the corpus card refuses exactly that. But the anchor record's applied note names only Darlings, so soul to soul was cut silently under the same authority. An unrecorded half-cut is indistinguishable from an oversight, and a later pass reading the record would have restored it. Recorded here as intentional; kept as cut. We mean this without contempt is the honest replacement for we mean it tenderly, since the address can promise the absence of contempt but cannot certify tenderness.

findings.summary: The three checkable grounds are better than the hidden-ache questions they replaced, and the finding runs the other way.

evidence.baseline: is it not true that beneath the will to own everything lies the same ache that lives in the rest of us — to be safe, to be seen, to rest somewhere that loves you back? Is it not, in the end, that we all just want a place to be **happy, healthy, and holy?**
evidence.shipped: We do not claim to know your inner life, and the appeal does not rest on a claim that every owner shares one hidden ache. It rests on three things you can check. On material interest: an owner of a beloved world sleeps, and an owner of a resentful one pays forever for the guarding of it. On moral responsibility: you will be the last people able to choose this cheaply. And on the generations not yet born, who inherit whatever we point the machine toward.

findings.authorizedBy: Not a defect. Recorded under R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT because the finding runs the other way.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline conscripts agreement twice by rhetorical question and claims access to the addressee's interior, which the corpus card names as defects in any register, and which is doubly wrong in an address to the people the volume has just audited: the claim that every owner secretly aches for love is exactly the kind of unfalsifiable assertion the volume's own register note forswears. The substitution names its grounds and makes each one checkable, and the second ground, you will be the last people able to choose this cheaply, is an argument the baseline never had. This is the strongest prior-pass contribution in the two addresses and it is credited at the same weight a loss would be.

findings.summary: The guard-cost sentence is better than the sleepless-owner prophecy it replaced, and the finding runs the other way.

evidence.baseline: The owner of a beloved world sleeps. The owner of an enslaved one never will.
evidence.shipped: an owner of a beloved world sleeps, and an owner of a resentful one pays forever for the guarding of it

findings.authorizedBy: Not a defect. Recorded under R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT because the finding runs the other way.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline pair is a curse: never will is a prophecy about another person's sleep, unfalsifiable and slightly gothic. The substitution names the mechanism, that a resented order pays a permanent guarding cost, which is a real observation from political economy and the material-interest ground stated concretely. Enslaved also overclaimed; resentful is the state the volume's evidence actually supports. The cost of the trade is the two-beat cadence of the baseline pair, which is noted and accepted: the material ground gains more from a checkable mechanism than it loses in rhythm, and the address still lands on its own strongest beat at the close.

findings.summary: The liturgical triad happy, healthy, and holy was deleted with the question that carried it, and only the question was recorded.

evidence.baseline: Is it not, in the end, that we all just want a place to be **happy, healthy, and holy?**

findings.authorizedBy: R-VOICE-BIND for the sentence; nothing recorded for the phrase.
findings.diagnosis: The sentence had to go: it tells all of us what we all want, in a rhetorical question, which the corpus card forbids twice over. But the triad itself was the only liturgical note in the first address, and it vanished as collateral rather than by decision. It is not named in any open canon query and appears nowhere else in the corpus, so R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD does not fire; the phrase is quoted here so the deletion is a recorded fact rather than an inference from a diff. Whether the triad is wanted somewhere card-compatible is an author question, listed below, not acted on.

findings.summary: Four universals were bounded by the restoration, and the bounds are kept.

evidence.baseline: the thing every human is starving for; No one has ever ruled a loveless world; a planet on which all affection has been enslaved out of existence; It is the most exquisite loneliness ever engineered.
evidence.shipped: the thing most human beings are hungry for; No one has yet ruled a loveless world; a planet on which affection has been engineered out of reach; It is an exquisite loneliness, and an expensive one.

findings.authorizedBy: Earn universals under section 5 of the standard, and catalog 4.6 on unsupported superlatives.
findings.diagnosis: Each reduction preserves the claim at the strength the argument supports. Every human starving was an interior universal; most human beings hungry is a bounded one the loneliness data in the reckoning actually back. Ever became yet, which keeps the historical claim and opens the door the address is holding open. Enslaved out of existence overclaimed and engineered out of reach names the mechanism. The superlative loneliness became an expensive one, which is not merely a reduction: expensive seeds the material-interest ground two sentences later. All four audited against the twenty rules and kept. R-CAUTIOUS-HALF was checked in the opposite direction: the committing content, are you happy there and the three-beat of what the machine cannot do, survived intact, so the bounding did not cost the address its falsifiable half.

findings.summary: One fund-list item has no baseline ancestor and is kept with its provenance visible.

evidence.baseline: Fund the good ideas — the medicine that heals rather than bills, the care that is honored, the food and soil and water held as commons rather than mined, the trust-network that circulates presence instead of harvesting it.
evidence.shipped: Fund the medicine that heals rather than bills, the care that is honored, the food and soil and water held as commons rather than mined, the technology answerable to the people it acts upon, the trust network that circulates presence instead of harvesting it.

findings.authorizedBy: Agent-seeded addition; recorded so the provenance stays visible, in the spirit of R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY.
findings.diagnosis: The technology answerable to the people it acts upon was written by the prior pass. It is kept because it restates a demand the volume makes in its own voice elsewhere, in the scored-trust section, where the risk is systems the affected person cannot inspect, contest, or leave, and in the three-roads section, where what decides is whether the limits can be enforced by the people the infrastructure acts upon. The list item coordinates the address with the diagnosis. But it is agent prose in an author's list, and the record says so rather than letting it pass as baseline. Fund the good ideas was dropped as a limb the list did not need; the list is the good ideas.

debtImpact.note: The address is framed as an address, invites rather than conscripts, and no longer rests on a claim about any owner's interior life. The label between evidence and address that the item requires is intact.
No declared protected line of the volume card lies inside this section. The card's protected lines were checked by string against the section before concluding this.

reasoning.note: The current text was derived from the baseline by the anchor pass and it survives the full twenty-rule derivation unchanged: the suppose-you-win frame, the question, the three-beat of what the machine cannot manufacture, the bolded triad to be loved, and to belong, and to have a place to be, the exquisite loneliness, the three checkable grounds, the fund list, and the close on people still in it who are glad you exist.

R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-REGISTER-DICTION, R-REFRAIN-COST, and R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT were run for the first time against this section. The first two found nothing to restore; the sweep results are recorded above. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE was checked against the card-authorized endearment cut and found the cut had silently widened to soul to soul, recorded in F1 and ratified rather than reversed. The substitution credits are F2 and F3. No refrain anchors in this section; the roof and stone refrains belong to the second address and Appendix B.

Punctuation already conformed: every baseline em dash in this section was resolved by the anchor pass to comma, colon, or period, and each repair was re-read against R-PUNCT-STRUCT. The colon before to be loved, and to belong, and to have a place to be genuinely specifies and stands.

openQuestions.question: Happy, healthy, and holy. The triad was deleted with the rhetorical question that carried it, correctly under the corpus card, but the phrase itself was the address's one liturgical note and it exists nowhere else in the corpus. If the author wants it, it needs a card-compatible carrier that asserts nothing about anyone's interior; if not, this record is its grave marker. Author decision; not acted on.

Soul to soul. Cut under the same authority as Darlings but never recorded until now. If the author considers the phrase load-bearing for the founder-to-founder posture, restoring it is a one-word-pair edit; the corpus card reading recorded in F1 argues against. Author decision; not acted on.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline under editorial/method/standard.md at the twenty-rule index ratified 2026-07-30, the corpus voice card, the volume-08 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS, with the substitution count taken before the pairing test and the paired-deletion sweep run before any restoration decision.
regenerationTest.conclusion: The derivation reproduces the shipped text. No new rule required. Two substitution credits recorded where the prior pass improved on the baseline, one silent half-cut ratified into the record, one agent-seeded list item kept with provenance visible.
